case: Medtronic / Covidien merger and corporate inversion (2015)

claude.performance_metric: ~$600M of targeted $850M synergies achieved by ~Aug 2017 (~30 months post-close); on track to $850M by FY2018
claude.rationale: Section 2 shows T4 (Covidien's product portfolio) and T5 (operational processes) both crossing the boundary and being integrated together to capture $850M synergies via combined supply-chain/manufacturing, so no product-vs-process mismatch at closing (gap_45=0). T5 process integration proceeded alongside T6 (combined ~85,000 people) as a full merger with a single leadership team, no documented process-vs-organization structural mismatch (gap_56=0). Section 3-4 document integration on plan (~$600M of ~$850M synergies by Aug 2017) with no product/process disruption (p4=0) and no process/organization fracture (p5=0). Business models were "complementary rather than substitutive" with limited overlap, and control consolidated under a single Ishrak-led team, so t1_archetype and t2_model are also 0.

grok.performance_metric: Integration on plan; ~$600M of $850M synergies by Aug 2017 (~2.5 years)
grok.rationale: Section 2 states T4 product portfolio transferred whole and complementary while T5 processes were integrated for synergies under the same new parent; no structural mismatch at closing. Sections 3-4 explicitly document no P4 or P5 disruption at 3-5yr horizon, with synergies delivered on plan and models described as complementary.
